page: Microsoft Azure E20ds_v7 is a memory-optimized cloud server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The virtual machine allocates 20 dedicated vCPUs spanning 10 physical cores with symmetric multithreading enabled. It features a tiered cache configuration comprising 48 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a substantial 480 MB L3 cache, backed by instruction support for Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) and AVX-512. The instance provisions 160 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Ephemeral storage is bundled directly via an integrated 1,182 GB local NVMe SSD, while discrete GPU acceleration is absent.

Benchmark results show competitive single-threaded computational and memory subsystem characteristics. In Geekbench testing, the instance achieved a strong single-core score of 1,983.0 and a multi-core score of 12,981.0, paired with strong single-threaded text processing of 2,754.0. Compression benchmarks demonstrated top-quartile throughput, recording 35.47 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 14.71 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Multi-core operations landed in the mid-range tier, including a multi-threaded stress-ng score of 20,081.26, a PassMark CPU score of 33,317.5, and static web serving throughput of 36.51 GB/sec. Large-block memory read throughput reached 141.96 GB/sec, supporting a Redis benchmark rate of 34.81 million SET operations per second.

The hardware configuration trades GPU compute capabilities for high memory density and high-speed temporary NVMe storage. This design offers resource efficiency for workloads bounded by memory footprint and I/O latency rather than raw parallel processor counts. The Microsoft Azure E20ds_v7 is technically well matched for relational databases, enterprise in-memory caches, big data extract-transform-load (ETL) routines, and analytical database management systems requiring rapid scratch space.
